threads.title: @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client npm `latest` tag points at 0.0.1-rc.1, so an unpinned `dsh plugin add` is rejected as incompatible
threads.bodyText:
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client on dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 fails:
dsh: installation rejected: Plugin @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.0.1-rc.1 is incompatible with dsh 0.2.1-rc.2: requirements {"@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm":"^0.0.1-rc.1","@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools":"^0.0.1-rc.1","@deepseek-ai/dsh-invariants":"^0.0.1-rc.1","@deepseek-ai/dsh-subprocess":"^0.0.1-rc.1"}. Running it may cause crashes or data loss. ...
dsh: nothing was installed.

Cause: the package's npm dist-tags are out of step with the rest of the scope, so an unpinned install resolves the first release candidate.
$ npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client dist-tags
{ latest: '0.0.1-rc.1', alpha: '0.2.1-alpha.5', next: '0.2.1-rc.3' }

$ npm view @deepseek-ai/dsh dist-tags
{ latest: '0.2.1-rc.2', alpha: '0.2.1-alpha.5', next: '0.2.1-rc.3' }

Workaround: pin the version.
dsh plugin --profile web add @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.1-rc.2

That installs cleanly, mounts from cordis.patch.yml, spawns the server at boot and registers its tools. Verified with chrome-devtools-mcp@1.12.0 (35 tools registered as mcp__chrome__*) on arm64 Linux, node 22, pnpm 12.
Suggested fix: npm dist-tag add @deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client@0.2.1-rc.2 latest.
Also, the install example in packages/mcp/mcp-client/README.md uses the bare package name, so it reproduces the failure for anyone who copies it until the tag is fixed. Happy to send a docs PR with a chrome-devtools-mcp example alongside the memory-server guide if that would be useful.

threads.title: [Bug] 升级至 0.2.1-rc.5 后，因第三方插件冲突导致启动崩溃 (1 required plugin did not activate)
threads.bodyText:
运行环境 (Environment)

OS: Windows 10 (10.0.19045.6466)
App Version: @deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop 0.2.1-rc.5
Electron: 44.7.0
Node.js: 24.21.0
安装方式: 桌面端自动更新（从旧版本更新至此版本）

问题描述 (Description)
更新至最新版本 0.2.1-rc.5 后，应用无法启动，直接闪退并弹出 "The application could not start or stopped unexpectedly" 报错。
通过查看崩溃日志发现，启动时因第三方插件（疑似之前安装的 @linxin666/dsh-web-all 等）与核心服务版本不兼容，导致核心服务 sessionProjections 注册失败。这引发了连锁反应，导致必须的核心插件 agent-loop 无法激活，最终导致 33 个依赖该服务的插件集体挂起，应用启动彻底失败。
崩溃日志 (Crash Log)
DesktopHostFatalError: dsh: startup failed: 1 required plugin did not activate

Plugins waiting for services (33):
  Plugin                     Missing services
  agent-loop (required)      sessionProjections
  session-title              sessionProjections
  session-title-llm          sessionTitle
  ... (以下省略)
"完整崩溃日志见附件：crash-2026-10-31T15-44-26-802Z-host.log"

###复现步骤 (Steps to Reproduce)
在旧版本中安装过第三方插件（如 @linxin666/dsh-web-all、dsh-better-sidebar 等）。
通过桌面端更新机制，升级到 0.2.1-rc.5 版本。
重启应用，直接报错闪退。

###临时解决办法 (Workaround)
目前通过“清空环境”恢复了运行。具体操作为：
彻底关闭应用及后台残留进程。
进入 .dsh\profiles\desktop 目录，将 package.json 中的 dependencies 清空为 {}。
删除 node_modules 文件夹。
重新执行 pnpm install，仅安装官方基础包。
应用可以成功启动，但代价是之前安装的所有第三方插件都被清空。

建议与诉求 (Suggestion)
理解第三方插件可能存在不兼容的情况，但目前这种“一个插件出错导致整个应用无法启动且没有 GUI 修复入口”的体验非常影响用户。
希望能：
在启动前加入插件兼容性校验，或者提供类似“安全模式/恢复模式”的启动选项（绕过用户插件）。
对于非 core 插件的异常，希望能做到“优雅降级”（如日志中出现的 plugin degraded），而不是直接阻断整个宿主程序的启动。
在更新提示中增加对第三方插件兼容性的警告。

感谢团队的辛勤付出！

threads.title: [Bug] Upgrading only @deepseek-ai/dsh* to 0.2.2-rc.1 leaves the cordis family at 4.0.x — pnpm exits 0, boot fails with version-unrelated errors
threads.bodyText:
Environment: Linux x86_64, Node v22.23.4 (see related note below), pnpm 12.10.1, DSH profile upgrading from 0.2.1-rc.5 to 0.2.2-rc.1 (web profile, ~325 deps, 44 bundles, a few local plugins).
Summary
When upgrading a profile to 0.2.2-rc.1, bumping only the @deepseek-ai/dsh* packages and forgetting the cordis family (@deepseek-ai/cordis, -plugin-group, -plugin-include, -plugin-loader, -plugin-timer, cosmokit, schemastery) produces a successful-looking install that only fails at boot, with errors that never mention a version. It would be very helpful if the upgrade guide called this out explicitly, and/or if the runtime asserted it.
What I did
# in a copy of the profile (production untouched)
sed -i 's/0\.2\.1-rc\.5/0.2.2-rc.1/g' package.json   # 282 @deepseek-ai/dsh* packages only
pnpm install --lockfile-only
Observed



check
result




pnpm install --lockfile-only
exit code 0, no error printed


cordis@4.1.0 occurrences in the lockfile
0


cordis@4.0.5 occurrences in the lockfile
1676


pnpm peers check
23 unmet peers, 6 of them are the cordis family itself



strict-peer-dependencies is off by default, so pnpm only warns. The installed tree then looks fine (pnpm list succeeds) and the profile boots into failures such as "a service is missing" / "configuration cannot be read" / "fiber config has an unexpected shape" — none of which point at @deepseek-ai/cordis.
Root cause
Every @deepseek-ai/dsh*@0.2.2-rc.1 package declares the cordis family as a peer, e.g.
$ tar -xOf dsh-agent-0.2.2-rc.1.tgz package/package.json | jq .peerDependencies
{ "@deepseek-ai/cordis": "~4.1.0", ... }

and the 0.2.2 release notes do mention "Update to Cordis Core 4.1.0, Loader 1.1.0, Include 1.1.0", but nothing in the upgrade path turns that into a hard failure: the dsh packages are upgraded by name (@deepseek-ai/dsh*), while the cordis packages are a different name pattern, so a scripted "bump all dsh packages" upgrade misses them by construction.
Suggested fixes (any one would help)

A startup assertion in app-boot: read the resolved @deepseek-ai/cordis version and fail loudly ("expected ~4.1.0, found 4.0.5 — upgrade the cordis family together with the engine") before mounting anything.
Upgrade guide: an explicit "these 7 packages must be upgraded in the same batch" list, next to the existing engines/plugin-API migration steps.
dsh doctor (or --dump-config) check: report unmet cordis-family peers, since pnpm's own warning is easy to lose in install output.

Workaround we use
Bump the cordis family in the same loop as the @deepseek-ai/dsh* packages, then verify:
grep -c 'cordis@4.1.0' pnpm-lock.yaml     # must be > 0
pnpm peers check                          # cordis-family entries must be gone
Why I'm reporting this
It cost us one "successful" dry run to notice, and the failure mode (install OK, boot broken, message unrelated to versions) is the kind of thing that is expensive to reproduce remotely. If the intended behavior is "users must bump both groups", a one-line assertion would save that.
